theme: 3 terms on standard-library protocols: stepping through values, reading items by position, and handing out values one by one

terms.definition: A protocol that lets a type hand out its values one at a time, so you can use it in a `for` loop.
terms.example: `Steps` is a Sequence, so I can use it directly in a `for` loop.

terms.definition: A protocol that lets a type be read many times by `index`, with a known `count` of items.
terms.example: An array is a Collection, so I can read the second tab by its `index`.

terms.definition: A protocol that gives out values one by one with `next()` and returns `nil` when none are left.
terms.example: My type follows IteratorProtocol, so `next()` returns `nil` after the last step.
terms.code:
var it = [10, 20].makeIterator()
print(it.next() ?? 0)
print(it.next() ?? 0)
print(it.next() as Any)

quizzes.question: In this code, which protocol requires the `next()` method?
What do you call the protocol that lets a `for` loop step through the values of a type?
What adds reading items by `index` and a `count` on top of stepping through them?

video.title: Sequence, Collection & IteratorProtocol | Day 33
video.description:
Learn to explain how Swift steps through values, reads items by index and hands out values one by one: Sequence, Collection & IteratorProtocol, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Sequence - A protocol that lets a type hand out its values one at a time, so you can use it in a `for` loop.
Collection - A protocol that lets a type be read many times by `index`, with a known `count` of items.
IteratorProtocol - A protocol that gives out values one by one with `next()` and returns `nil` when none are left.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Sequence, Collection & IteratorProtocol in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
시퀀스, 컬렉션, 이터레이터 프로토콜 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Sequence - A protocol that lets a type hand out its values one at a time, so you can use it in a `for` loop.
한국어: 시퀀스: 값을 하나씩 내어 주어 `for` 루프에서 쓸 수 있게 해 주는 프로토콜

Collection - A protocol that lets a type be read many times by `index`, with a known `count` of items.
한국어: 컬렉션: `index`로 여러 번 읽을 수 있고 항목 `count`를 아는 타입을 위한 프로토콜

IteratorProtocol - A protocol that gives out values one by one with `next()` and returns `nil` when none are left.
한국어: 이터레이터 프로토콜: `next()`로 값을 하나씩 주고 더 없으면 `nil`을 돌려주는 프로토콜

landscape.hook: Can you explain these loop terms in English?

dialogue.title: Can I loop over Steps?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, can I use `Steps` in a `for` loop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, it is a Sequence, so a `for` loop can step through it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does the Sequence know the next value?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It uses IteratorProtocol. The `next()` method gives one value each time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And what happens when the values run out?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then `next()` returns `nil`, and the loop stops. That is the IteratorProtocol rule.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. Can I jump to the third step by `index`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not with a plain Sequence. For `index` you need Collection.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wait, I thought a Sequence already gave me an `index`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not quite. Collection adds `index`, and you can read it many times.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Sequence for the loop, Collection for the `index`.
Make it a Sequence, and a `for` loop works.
